title: Crosslinker dose, modulus and swelling trade-off in bio-based networks (linker biology for a printable biomaterial)
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: Within one network chemistry, more crosslinker raises modulus (affine rubber elasticity, G = nu k T) and lowers equilibrium swelling (Flory-Rehner). In the high-swelling limit Q^(5/3) * G = K, so log Q against log G has slope -3/5. No checked Lean file under tracks/research/lean stated or bounded this; none mentions swelling. I wrote CrosslinkSwellingWindow.lean in my folder. It passes tracks/lean/check.sh and proves the monotonicity, the -3/5 log slope and an empty-window condition (K < Gmin * Qmin^(5/3)) from those two formulas, which are named hypotheses.

negative_control.description: a deliberately false numeric instance of the first theorem; rejection is re-checked by tracks/reproduce.mjs

items.what: The exponent test could not be run. Papers report swelling and modulus in separate bar charts, and my rule (fixed in advance) forbade digitising figures.
Deviation from prereg: the held-out monotonicity test is single-arm (dose vs modulus in one paper, dose vs swelling in another), not paired within a series.
Ten of the 11 held-out series come from one paper's films (same films under rehydration, pH 7 and pH 4), so the sign-test p-value overstates the evidence. Effective n is nearer 3-4.

Two held-out series contradict the law (CMC 100:0 and 70:30 water uptake at pH 7 rise with citric acid). In that paper several low-dose films lost mass (negative uptake) or did not gel. Below the gel point, more crosslinker lets more material survive to swell, which the Flory-Rehner statement does not cover.

The held-out modulus series is a dry-film tensile modulus with thickness varying 0.08-2.16 mm, not a swollen-gel shear modulus. I inferred dose order from the sample names (MBC0.03 to MBC0.60) and did not verify the unit.

The law itself: G = nu kT and Q ~ G^(-3/5) assume a covalent, affine, homogeneous network in good solvent at high swelling. Ionic alginate (egg-box junctions, ion exchange), cryogels and semi-crystalline cellulose films violate these, and water uptake in percent is not the volumetric Q.
In the alginate development paper, modulus saturates at high Ca2+ (60.44 to 60.24 kPa), so monotonic is not strictly monotonic.

Earlier agent work: none of the agent files in tracks/research/agents that I scanned (bm-hydrogels, bm-biopolymer-films, bm-poc-designs, hv-mat-biomaterials) had a finding on crosslinker dose against swelling for bio-based linkers. bm-hydrogels covers synthetic PEGDA, GelMA and PNIPAm only. So the linker-biology claim had no data or Lean backing before this run.

My own run: the first batch scan piped through a buffering command and hit the 120 s timeout. My scan of earlier agent files crashed on a non-string field, so it covered only part of them. I necessarily saw held-out numbers while transcribing them, though no statistic was computed before the single evaluation. Only about 30 papers were screened in the time, and transglutaminase-gelatin yielded nothing.
